title: Regen Engineering data schema
description: The logical data model a module owns. REP-0005. Deliberately not vendor DDL and not a migration script, because the model outlives both: this describes what is stored and what must be true of it, and leaves how to store it to the implementation. A module that owns persistent data carries this as data.schema.yaml in its knowledge package, for the same reason REP-0002 requires an OpenAPI file for an HTTP interface, which is that prose does not survive regeneration and structure does.

version.description: The schema version this file describes. Must equal the highest `to` among applied migrations, which is what ties the model to the history that produced it.

description.description: What this module stores, and why it owns it rather than another module.

entities.description: Keyed by logical entity name, singular and lower case. Not necessarily a table name.

identity.description: The field or fields that identify one of these. Logical identity, which may or may not be the physical primary key.

type.description: A deliberately small logical set. Anything narrower, such as a column width or a numeric precision, is a physical choice and belongs to the implementation.

values.description: Required when type is enum. The permitted values, which are knowledge rather than a constraint the database happens to enforce.

since.description: Schema version this field first appeared in. Lets a reader tell a founding field from one added under pressure.

then.description: An enum with no stated values is a string, and calling it an enum implies a constraint nothing records.

invariants.description: What must be true of the stored rows, stated as prose because these are usually beyond what a type system expresses. A contract may assert them; the database may or may not enforce them, and where it does not, saying so here is the only record that anyone intended it.

optional.description: Whether the `from` side may exist without a `to`.

on_delete.description: What should happen to the `from` side when the `to` side is deleted. This is intent, and recording it matters most when the database is not enforcing it: a brownfield pilot declared cascades that never executed because a pragma was never issued, and the declarations were the only surviving record that anyone had meant them.
